Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until

# demo two input-output differences
I='''9 9 0 0 9 0 0 9 9 9 9 9
9 9 9 0 9 0 0 9 9 9 9 0
9 9 9 0 0 9 0 9 9 9 9 9
0 9 9 0 9 9 9 9 0 0 9 9
0 0 9 0 9 9 9 0 0 0 9 0

9 9 9 0 0 9 9 0 9 9 0 9
0 0 0 0 0 9 0 9 9 9 0 0
0 0 0 0 0 9 0 0 9 9 9 9
0 0 9 0 9 9 9 0 9 9 9 9'''
a=[list(map(int,x.split())) for x in I.splitlines()]
# components of 0, print comps colored in output = those 0s in output replaced by 5; known locations from demo visually
for mode in (4,8):
 seen=set(); comps=[]
 for r in range(13):
  for c in range(12):
   if a[r][c]!=0 or (r,c) in seen:continue
   st=[(r,c)];seen.add((r,c));q=[]
   while st:
    x,y=st.pop();q.append((x,y))
    for dx in [-1,0,1]:
     for dy in [-1,0,1]:
      if not (dx or dy) or (mode==4 and dx and dy):continue
      z=(x+dx,y+dy)
      if 0<=z[0]<13 and 0<=z[1]<12 and a[z[0]][z[1]]==0 and z not in seen:seen.add(z);st.append(z)
   comps.append(q)
 print('mode',mode,[(len(q),(min(r for r,c in q),min(c for r,c in q),max(r for r,c in q),max(c for r,c in q))) for q in comps if len(q)>3])
